topics.label: Latency vs Throughput
topics.desc: The core tension between per-request response time and aggregate work per second, which optimizations trade off against each other.

topics.label: Tail Latency
topics.desc: High-percentile (p95/p99) response times that dominate user experience and fan-out behavior even when the mean looks healthy.

topics.label: Little's Law
topics.desc: The relation L = λW linking concurrency, arrival rate, and latency, used to reason about queue sizes and capacity.

topics.label: Queueing Theory
topics.desc: Models like M/M/1 explaining how utilization drives nonlinear latency growth and why systems collapse near saturation.

topics.label: Universal Scalability Law
topics.desc: Gunther's model adding contention and coherency penalties to Amdahl's law, predicting where added capacity stops helping.

topics.label: Amdahl's Law
topics.desc: The bound on speedup from parallelization set by the serial fraction of work, framing limits of optimization effort.

topics.label: Saturation & Bottlenecks
topics.desc: Identifying the single constraining resource (CPU, I/O, memory, locks) that gates throughput per the theory of constraints.

topics.label: CPU Profiling
topics.desc: Sampling or instrumenting call stacks to attribute CPU time to functions and find hot paths worth optimizing.

topics.label: Flame Graphs
topics.desc: Brendan Gregg's stacked visualization of sampled stacks that makes dominant code paths and their callers instantly legible.

topics.label: Sampling vs Instrumentation
topics.desc: The trade-off between low-overhead statistical sampling and exact-but-intrusive instrumentation when collecting profiles.

topics.label: Memory Profiling
topics.desc: Heap and allocation analysis to find leaks, churn, and oversized objects that drive GC pressure and footprint.

topics.label: Benchmarking
topics.desc: Repeatable measurement of code or system performance under controlled load, the empirical basis for any optimization claim.

topics.label: Microbenchmark Pitfalls
topics.desc: Dead-code elimination, JIT warmup, and constant folding that make naive microbenchmarks measure nothing real.

topics.label: Continuous Profiling
topics.desc: Always-on, low-overhead production profiling (e.g. Parca, Pyroscope) giving fleet-wide cost attribution over time.

topics.label: Algorithmic Optimization
topics.desc: Choosing better complexity classes and data structures, usually the largest and most durable performance win available.

topics.label: Data Locality
topics.desc: Arranging memory access to exploit cache lines and prefetching, often dwarfing instruction-count concerns on modern CPUs.

topics.label: Batching & Coalescing
topics.desc: Amortizing fixed per-operation overhead by grouping work, trading a little latency for large throughput gains.

topics.label: Lazy vs Eager Evaluation
topics.desc: Deferring or precomputing work to match the access pattern, avoiding wasted computation or amortizing it upfront.

topics.label: Memoization
topics.desc: Caching pure-function results keyed by inputs to trade memory for repeated recomputation of expensive deterministic work.

topics.label: I/O & Syscall Reduction
topics.desc: Cutting context switches and round trips via buffering, zero-copy, and async I/O when work is I/O-bound rather than CPU-bound.

topics.label: Parallelization
topics.desc: Exploiting multiple cores via threads, vectorization, or pipelining to cut wall-clock time on parallelizable workloads.

topics.label: Premature Optimization
topics.desc: Knuth's warning that optimizing before measuring wastes effort and complexity on code that isn't the bottleneck.

topics.label: Cache Levels & Tiers
topics.desc: Layering caches from CPU to CDN, each trading capacity for latency, with hit rate as the central effectiveness metric.

topics.label: Eviction Policies
topics.desc: LRU, LFU, ARC, and W-TinyLFU strategies deciding what to drop when a cache fills, directly setting the hit rate.

topics.label: Cache Invalidation
topics.desc: Keeping cached data correct via TTLs, write-through, or explicit purges — famously one of the hardest problems in computing.

topics.label: Caching Patterns
topics.desc: Cache-aside, read-through, write-through, and write-behind strategies that define how reads and writes flow through a cache.

topics.label: Cache Stampede
topics.desc: The thundering herd when a hot key expires and many requests recompute it at once, mitigated by locking or early refresh.

topics.label: Content Delivery Networks
topics.desc: Edge caches replicating static and dynamic content near users to cut latency and offload origin servers.

topics.label: Distributed Cache Consistency
topics.desc: Keeping replicated caches in sync across nodes, balancing staleness against the cost of coordination and invalidation traffic.

topics.label: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling
topics.desc: Scaling up with bigger machines versus out with more nodes, the foundational axis of every capacity decision.

topics.label: Load Balancing
topics.desc: Distributing requests across replicas via round-robin, least-connections, or hashing to spread load and avoid hotspots.

topics.label: Stateless Services
topics.desc: Externalizing session state so any node can serve any request, the precondition for trivial horizontal scaling.

topics.label: Autoscaling
topics.desc: Adding or removing capacity automatically from load signals, balancing responsiveness against thrashing and cost.

topics.label: Capacity Planning
topics.desc: Forecasting resource needs from growth and headroom targets so the system stays off the steep part of the latency curve.

topics.label: Backpressure
topics.desc: Propagating overload upstream so producers slow down rather than building unbounded queues that collapse the system.

topics.label: Load Shedding
topics.desc: Deliberately dropping or degrading low-priority work under overload to protect overall availability and core flows.

topics.label: Sharding for Scale
topics.desc: Partitioning data and traffic by key so each shard handles a slice, the standard route past single-node write limits.

topics.label: Three Pillars
topics.desc: Metrics, logs, and traces as complementary telemetry types, the conventional framing for what to instrument.

topics.label: Structured Logging
topics.desc: Emitting machine-parseable key-value logs so events can be queried, filtered, and correlated rather than grepped.

topics.label: Metric Types
topics.desc: Counters, gauges, histograms, and summaries, each suited to different signals and aggregation semantics over time.

topics.label: Distributed Tracing
topics.desc: Following a request across services via propagated context and spans to expose where latency and errors originate.

topics.label: Context Propagation
topics.desc: Carrying trace and baggage identifiers across process and network boundaries so spans stitch into one coherent trace.

topics.label: OpenTelemetry
topics.desc: The vendor-neutral standard and SDKs for generating and exporting metrics, logs, and traces with a common data model.

topics.label: Cardinality Management
topics.desc: Controlling label dimensionality, since unbounded tag combinations explode storage cost and degrade query performance.

topics.label: Trace Sampling
topics.desc: Head- or tail-based selection of which traces to keep, balancing diagnostic coverage against volume and cost.

topics.label: Four Golden Signals
topics.desc: Latency, traffic, errors, and saturation as the minimal dashboard set Google's SRE book prescribes for any service.

topics.label: SLIs, SLOs & SLAs
topics.desc: Indicators, internal objectives, and contractual agreements that turn reliability into measurable, defensible targets.

topics.label: Error Budgets
topics.desc: The allowed unreliability from an SLO, spent to balance feature velocity against stability in a data-driven way.

topics.label: Alerting Design
topics.desc: Defining actionable, low-noise alerts on symptoms not causes so on-call engineers trust and act on every page.

topics.label: Alert Fatigue
topics.desc: The desensitization from noisy or non-actionable alerts that causes real incidents to be missed or ignored.

topics.label: Dashboards & Visualization
topics.desc: Curated views (e.g. Grafana) that surface golden signals and trends so humans can spot anomalies and triage fast.

topics.label: Synthetic & RUM
topics.desc: Active synthetic probes plus real-user monitoring giving complementary outside-in and field views of availability.

topics.label: Anomaly Detection
topics.desc: Statistical or ML baselining that flags deviations automatically when static thresholds can't capture normal variation.

topics.label: Incident Response
topics.desc: The structured process of detecting, triaging, and resolving production outages to restore service quickly and safely.

topics.label: Incident Command
topics.desc: Roles like commander, comms, and scribe (from ICS) that coordinate responders and prevent chaos during major incidents.

topics.label: On-Call Practice
topics.desc: Rotations, escalation policies, and runbooks that make production ownership sustainable and humane for engineers.

topics.label: Blameless Postmortems
topics.desc: Structured retrospectives focused on systemic causes over individual blame so the org actually learns from failure.

topics.label: Root Cause Analysis
topics.desc: Techniques like Five Whys and contributing-factor analysis to find the deep causes behind an incident's symptoms.

topics.label: MTTR & Reliability Metrics
topics.desc: MTTD, MTTR, MTBF, and change-fail rate quantifying how fast and how often a team detects, recovers, and breaks things.

topics.label: Chaos Engineering
topics.desc: Deliberately injecting failures in production to validate resilience assumptions before real outages expose them.

topics.label: Game Days & DiRT
topics.desc: Rehearsed disaster drills that exercise runbooks, tooling, and human coordination so real incidents go smoothly.

topics.label: Observability vs Monitoring
topics.desc: The distinction between asking known questions (monitoring) and exploring unknown-unknowns from rich telemetry (observability).
